en: Only now do I live in worth in my own eyes, since my sinful eye sees
the pure land and the soil as well
to which people ascribe so much honour.
What I always prayed for has come to pass:
I have come to the place where God walked in human form.
Beautiful lands, rich and splendid,
whatever of them I have seen so far,
you are the honour of them all.
What a wonder has happened here!
That a maiden bore a child,
lord over all the host of angels:
was that not a wonder entirely?
Here he, the pure one, let himself be baptised,
so that mankind might be pure.
Then he let himself be sold here,
so that we who were bondsmen became free.
Otherwise we would have been lost.
Hail to you, spear, cross and thorn!
Woe to you [?] ... that is your wrath [?]
When he wished to have mercy on us,
then he suffered the cruel death,
he, so mighty, for us who were so poor,
so that we might come out of our distress. That it did not irk him then,
that is a wonder far too great, surpassing all wonders.
From here the Son went to hell,
from the grave in which he lay.
In this the Father was ever his companion [?],
and the Spirit, whom no one can
set apart: it is one,
straight and smoother than an arrow-shaft,
as he appeared to Abraham.
When he had so put the devil to shame
that no emperor ever fought better,
then he came back here to the land.
Then the grief of the Jews began:
that he, the lord, broke through their guard,
and that he was seen alive afterwards,
he whom their hand struck and pierced.
In this land he has pronounced
a fearful day, when the orphan will be avenged
and the widow may bring her complaint,
and the poor man the violence that was done to them.
Well for him there who made amends here.
Our local judges' scheming delays no one's suit there,
for he will judge there at once:
so it is on the last day.
And whoever leaves any debt here
unsettled, how will he fare
there, where he has neither pledge nor guarantor?
Do not let it weary you,
what I have said so far;
now I will unlock the matter
briefly, and also make it known:
whatever God ever did with the world,
that began there and ends here.
After that he was in the land
forty days; then he went there, whence his Father sent him.
His Spirit, may he keep us:
that he sent back at once.
Holy is that same land,
its name is known before God.
Christians, Jews and the heathens
say that this is their inheritance.
May God judge it rightly
by his three names.
All the world fights here; we are in the right claim.
It is right that he grant it to us.
notes: The text is a diplomatic transcription of one manuscript (folio change [126v] in line 8.5 is left out of the translation); its wording differs in places from the usual critical editions, and the translation follows what this manuscript has.

line 3.7: 'wie dir ze den ist din zorn' does not construe as written; it looks like a corrupt copy of a line cursing the heathens ('woe to you, heathens, that grieves you'). Rendered with [?]; the editor may prefer to leave the line marked as unclear.

line 5.3: 'dest der vanter ie geselle' is corrupt ('vanter' for 'vater'); read as 'in this the Father was ever his companion', i.e. the Father did not leave the Son in the harrowing of hell. Uncertain.
line 5.6: 'zein' is a rod or arrow-shaft; the image (the Trinity as one, straighter and smoother than a shaft) is the poem's own.
line 1.1: 'mir werde' = 'worthy to myself', i.e. my life now has worth in my own eyes.
line 3.4: 'eigen' = unfree people, bondsmen (as opposed to 'fri', free).
line 8.1: 'lantrehter tihten' read as 'the scheming/devising of our local judges'; the sense is that earthly courts' delays count for nothing at the Last Judgement. 'vristet' = postpones.
line 8.4: 'schulde' covers both debt and guilt.
line 9.6: this manuscript has 'dort ... hie' ('began there and ends here'); the sense is that God's dealings with the world began and end in this land.
line 10.3: 'er vns bewar' read as a wish, 'may he keep us'; other copies have a relative clause ('who may keep us').
line 11.4: 'by his three names' = by the Trinity.
line 11.5: 'ger' = desire or claim (also a spear); read as 'we are in the right in our claim'.
